name: Portsmouth steam-powered block mill
summary: At Portsmouth dockyard a line of steam-driven machines made pulley blocks for the navy's rigging in sequence, an early model of machine-based mass production.
description: Brunel-designed, Maudslay-built sequence of steam-driven machines for producing naval rigging blocks at Portsmouth.
tier_reason: Prefer promotion for an integrated production system, distinguishing the system from each surviving constituent machine. This is a scoped consequence judgement, not a reward for documentation or representation.
why: The Royal Navy needed very large numbers of rigging blocks during the wars with France, and hand-making them was slow and costly.

date.label: 1803 initial operation
date.basis: The Historic England building chronology states that the first set of Brunel’s machines was operational in 1803. The Navy survey reports steam-powered operation by 1803.

events.statement: The Navy’s Portsmouth block-making machinery was operating by 1803 with steam power and sequential specialist machinery.
events.caveats: One installed set operated by 1803; this is not a claim the whole system was complete then or the first mechanized production worldwide.

evidence.locator: Printed pp.63–64, Mechanised and powered sawing
